scope: offline subprocess crash-cut composition of retained durable authority token state with existing durable-submit pre-transport journal; injected transport only; no model, GUI, OS input, or network
H: Naive serial composition token.consume() -> durable_submit.run(command) leaves an inter-journal crash cut in which the authority token is durably consumed but durable-submit has no pending request identity. After durable-submit has committed its pending record, the existing journal should preserve explicit delivery uncertainty and refuse blind new-command replay.
T: Use byte-identified current-main durable_token_state_v2 plus the minimal durable_submit_v1 core contract, whose pre-transport sequencing is retained by v6. Run separate-process cuts: pending/no submit; crash after token consume before durable-submit call; crash in injected transport after durable-submit pending commit; restart new-command refusal and read-only timeout after that crash; reverse-order control where submit reaches transport while token remains pending. One frozen first-outcome matrix, no tuning/retry.
D: RETAIN_COMPOSITION_BOUNDARY if consume-before-submit crash yields token=consumed and submit.pending=null, while transport-crash yields submit.pending.write_state=may_have_been_sent and later new command is refused before transport. Reverse-order must demonstrate that submit-before-consume is not a valid token gate. HOLD exactly-once/atomic-composition claims.
C: An existing prepare-only or effect-owner idempotency contract could eliminate the inter-journal gap; none was found in the durable-submit run path before freeze. This experiment does not add such a protocol.
U: Single writer, local filesystem, process crash and injected replies only; no power-loss, runtime crash, hostile checkpoint, live GUI, or model claim.
